s1.syndrome_frame: Acute vision loss in one eye following a traumatic incident to the head
salient_findings: History of being struck by lightning to the forehead
Central macular thickening and posterior subcapsular cataract development in the affected eye over time
Intraretinal cystoid changes and subfoveal ellipsoid zone disruption on OCT
key_facts: Patient is a white woman in her 20s
Unremarkable medical and ocular history
Symptoms began 4 days prior to presentation
Struck by lightning directly to the right forehead
Uncorrected visual acuity measured 20/50 OD and 20/20 OS
Pupils were symmetric, with no relative afferent pupillary defect
Initial anterior segment examination was normal
Initial dilated fundus examination showed no apparent abnormalities in either eye
Central macular thickening developed in the right eye by 2 weeks
Mild posterior subcapsular cataract visible in the right eye by 7 weeks
OCT showed subtle irregularity of the outer retinal layers in the right eye initially
OCT showed intraretinal cystoid changes and subfoveal ellipsoid zone disruption in the right eye at 2 weeks
OCT showed restoration of foveal contour with decreased cystoid abnormalities and further loss of outer retinal layers by 7 weeks

shortlist.label: Purtscher-like retinopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Trauma to the head and subsequent vision loss are consistent with this condition

shortlist.label: Commotio retinae
shortlist.why_kept: Berlin's edema is a form of commotio retinae, which is a common cause of vision loss after head trauma

shortlist.label: Traumatic optic neuropathy
shortlist.why_kept: Direct trauma to the forehead could have caused optic nerve damage

shortlist.label: Lightning-induced cataract
shortlist.why_kept: The patient was struck by lightning, which could have caused cataract formation

shortlist.label: Traumatic retinal pigment epitheliopathy
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's OCT findings and vision loss are consistent with this condition

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms and OCT findings, including central macular thickening, intraretinal cystoid changes, and subfoveal ellipsoid zone disruption, are consistent with Purtscher-like retinopathy, which can occur after traumatic injuries, including those caused by lightning strikes.

rejected.label: Commotio retinae
rejected.why: Commotio retinae typically presents with retinal edema and hemorrhages, which were not noted in the initial examination.

rejected.label: Traumatic optic neuropathy
rejected.why: There was no relative afferent pupillary defect, which is often seen in traumatic optic neuropathy.

rejected.label: Lightning-induced cataract
rejected.why: While a cataract did develop, the primary issue was the retinal changes, not the cataract.

rejected.label: Traumatic retinal pigment epitheliopathy
rejected.why: The OCT findings and clinical presentation do not specifically suggest damage to the retinal pigment epithelium as the primary issue.
